Secrets Unveiled! Properties 40-90% Below Market Value – Moore County, North Carolina Tax Deed Investing

Step into the world of real estate opportunity in Moore County, North Carolina! Imagine securing dirt-cheap properties through the County’s Tax Foreclosure Sale, a dynamic event held right on the steps of the courthouse.

How to Get Started with Tax Deed Investing in Moore County:

  1. Stay Updated: Monitor Zacchaeus Legal Services for the next sale date. There’s no set schedule, so staying informed through their updates is crucial.
  2. Attend the Auction: Head to the Moore County Courthouse. Bidding doesn’t require pre-registration, so just show up prepared.
  3. Financial Preparation: Winning a bid requires an immediate 20% deposit, payable in cash or certified check. The bid remains open for ten days for any upset bids. If you’re still the highest bidder after this period, the full payment is due within 30 days. Ensure you have your finances in order, as all payments must be in certified funds.
  4. Recording the Deed: After full payment, recording the deed at the Register of Deeds office is your responsibility.

Important Details for Moore County Tax Deed Sales:

Additional Information

  • Foreclosures: The Moore County Tax Department initiates foreclosure proceedings if property taxes are past due. Properties may then be auctioned publicly.
  • Sale Notices: Notices are posted two consecutive weeks before the sale date.
  • Finances: Ensure funding is available before bidding. All sales must be paid with certified funds.

Fun Facts About Moore County:

  • Population: 97,264​.
  • Notable Areas: Known for its beautiful golf courses, including Pinehurst, the home of major golf tournaments.
  • Historical Significance: Moore County is home to the famous Pinehurst Resort, a historic landmark.

Pro Tips:

  • Research: Always check the property details on Zacchaeus Legal Services before bidding.
  • Stay Ready: Ensure you have the necessary funds and deposit amount for a smooth transaction.
  • Upset Bids: Be aware that other bidders may challenge your offer within the 10-day period after the auction.

FAQ

  1. How can I get a list of the properties being sold?

    The Moore County Clerk of Superior Court’s Office posts listings on the bulletin board, and The Pilot Newspaper includes them in the classified legal ads section. They typically post about four weeks prior to the sale date.
  2. How do they conduct foreclosure sales?

    Zacchaeus Legal Services conducts the sales in the lobby of the Moore County Courts Facility, auctioning properties to the highest bidder.
  3. Do I have to be present to bid on a tax foreclosure property?

    Yes, you or a representative should be present to place a bid. The Moore County Clerk of Court’s office handles upset bids, keeping the bid open for 10 days.
  4. How often do they Conduct tax foreclosure sales?

    There is no set schedule. Zacchaeus Legal Services posts sale dates on their website.
  5. Can I buy tax liens in North Carolina?

    No, buying tax liens is not legal in North Carolina. Recorded deeds or will transfer property ownership.
